observations: Multiple electronic keyboards leaning against a wall, wrapped in clear plastic film.
The keyboards appear to be used, with some showing signs of wear on the plastic wrap.
The keyboards are of various colors (black, white, grey, blue).
A box for a 'KORG' brand keyboard is visible in the background of photo 0.
The keyboards have a standard 61-key layout.
The brand name 'KORG' is visible on the control panel in photo 2.

claims.evidence: The plastic wrap obscures the condition of the keys and the internal electronics.
This is a subjective claim about value and cannot be verified through photos.

claims.claim: All keys and buttons working, adapter included. Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The plastic wrap may have hidden cracks or tears that affect the keyboard's internal condition.
risks.proof: A photo of the keyboard with the plastic wrap removed.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not power on or produce sound.
risks.proof: A video of the keyboard being powered on and producing audio.

risks.risk: The keyboard may have a faulty or missing power adapter.
risks.proof: A photo of the power adapter and a video showing it is connected.

risks.risk: The keyboard may have a dead key or a broken button.
risks.proof: A video of a full key press test.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the keyboard with the plastic wrap removed.
Video of the keyboard powered on and playing a demo song.
Photo of the model number sticker on the keyboard.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
